name: Marah
overview: Marah represents the first challenge the Israelites faced after crossing the Red Sea, where they found no water for three days in the wilderness before encountering the bitter waters at Marah. The bitterness of the water caused the people to murmur against Moses, questioning what they would drink. In response, Moses cried out to the LORD, who showed him a tree to cast into the waters, making them sweet and drinkable. This event not only provided physical sustenance but also served as a test of faith, where God established a statute and ordinance for His people.
